key_insight: Agentic source analysis can turn a sprawling set of logic-optimization operators into a smaller, theory-derived subset with exact admission rules.
engineering_relevance: For synthesis toolflows like ABC and mockturtle, this enables faster orchestration with fewer operators while preserving bit-identical results and improving area/depth outcomes.
method: LLM agents read pinned ABC and mockturtle source code to infer operator-level relations and their valid scope.
Adversarial audits test each claimed relation against implementation guards, bounds, and update-order details.
Certified relations are compiled into deterministic gates and used to compress the operator set in ABC Orchestrate (TACO).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 40 deployed recipe actions compressed to a 31-action exact Pareto cover; two exact gates cut Orchestrate runtime by 11% on 66 circuits, and TACO was 2.6x faster with modest node/level reductions in a held-fixed comparison.
watch_item: The gates are exact for the audited implementations, but portability may depend on source-version changes, hidden guards, or backend-specific behavior.
paper_title: Rethinking Logic Optimization Operators: Theory-Derived Operator Compression via Agentic Source Analysis
